scenes.title: Opposites, Inflections and Correlatives
scenes.summary: The first topics: from opposites, as in the Messenian Speech and two tragic passages; from like inflections; and from correlatives, as Diomedon argued about the taxes, with the caution that doer and sufferer must be judged apart, as in Theodectes' Alcmaeon and the cases of Nicanor and of the man killed at Thebes.

scenes.title: More and Less, Time, and the Opponent's Words
scenes.summary: From the more and the less, as “if not even the gods know everything”; from equal cases, as Oeneus, Theseus and Alexander; from time, as Iphicrates claimed his statue and Philip passage through Boeotia; and from turning the opponent's words against him, as Iphicrates did to Aristophon.

scenes.title: Definition, Senses, Division and Induction
scenes.summary: From definition, as Socrates on his divine sign, Iphicrates on nobility and Socrates on Archelaus; from the number of senses; from division; and from induction, as mothers settled paternity at Athens and Thebes, and in Theodectes' Law and Alcidamas' list of cities that honored the wise.

scenes.title: Previous Judgments and Parts
scenes.summary: From a previous judgment of the gods, the wise or the judges, as Autocles cited the Dread Goddesses, Sappho the gods, Aristippus Socrates, Hegesipolis Zeus, and Isocrates Theseus, the goddesses and Conon; and from the parts, as in Theodectes' Socrates.

scenes.title: Consequences, Analogy and Changing Choices
scenes.summary: From consequences, as education brings envy and wisdom, the whole art of Callippus; from opposite consequences, as the priestess and her son; from what is praised openly and wished in private; from analogy, as Iphicrates' son and Theodectes on the mercenaries; from identical consequences, as Xenophanes on the gods; and from changes of choice.

scenes.title: Motives, Incentives and the Incredible
scenes.summary: From the possible motive, as in two tragedies and Theodectes' Ajax; from incentives and deterrents, the whole art of Pamphilus and Callippus; and from the incredible, as Androcles argued that the laws need a law.

scenes.title: Inconsistency, Causes, Mistakes and Names
scenes.summary: From inconsistency; from the cause of a false impression, as the mother and Theodectes' Odysseus; from cause and effect, as Leodamas answered Thrasybulus; from a better course; from contrary acts, as Xenophanes advised the people of Elea; from mistakes, as in Carcinus' Medea, the art of Theodorus; and from names, as Conon, Herodicus, Euripides and Chaeremon played on them.

scenes.title: Which Enthymemes Are Admired
scenes.summary: Refutative enthymemes are more admired than demonstrative ones, and the most applauded are those the hearers foresee, or grasp as soon as they are said.
